renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: top_variable_heatmap
  title: Most variable genes across samples
  description: |-
    Each cell is a gene in one sample: its expression as log2(TPM + 1), with genes as rows and samples as columns. It answers which genes separate the samples and whether replicates group together.
    How to read: columns of one condition that cluster together and share a pattern mean the experiment is reproducible. A replicate that clusters away from its group is a candidate outlier, so check the sample overview. Rows with the same pattern across samples are co-regulated genes, the first candidates for a signature.
    Lines and annotations: the coloured bar above the columns is the experimental factor read from the sample sheet or the sample names, and rows and columns are clustered with the tile's default Ward linkage. The matrix holds the 500 genes with the highest variance, a fixed selection of this view.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: gene_name

- component: table
  title: Most variable genes table
  description: |-
    Each row is one of the most variable genes with its log2(TPM + 1) in every sample. It answers what the heatmap colours stand for in numbers.
    How to read: sort a sample column to find the genes it expresses most, and search a gene symbol to read its values across samples.

- component: figure
  title: Expression by group
  description: |-
    Each box is a group of samples: the distribution of log2(TPM + 1) over the genes expressed in at least one sample. It answers whether groups share the same overall expression level.
    How to read: boxes at similar heights mean comparable libraries. A box shifted up or down points to a global difference in expression or in library composition, so check the sample overview before a differential analysis. Pick genes in the filter to see one gene across groups.
    Lines and annotations: genes are kept when at least one sample reaches 1 TPM, a fixed filter of this view and not a Salmon cut-off. The dashed line is the median log2(TPM + 1) of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Salmon.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: group
    y: log2_tpm
    color: group
    labels:
      group: Group
      log2_tpm: Expression (log2 TPM + 1)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log2_tpm

- component: card
  title: Expression level
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log2(TPM + 1) over every gene and sample in view, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how strongly the typical gene is expressed.
    How to read: raw TPM spans orders of magnitude, so the log scale is used here. Filter to one gene or group to compare levels.
  column: log2_tpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Genes in view
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes in view, and the bars rank the groups by how many genes they carry rows for. It answers how many genes the explorer holds.
    How to read: the table holds genes expressed in at least one sample, so the count is the same across groups unless a filter is applied.
  column: gene_name
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: genes, by group

- component: interactive
  title: Gene picker
  description: |-
    Pick one or more genes to restrict every tile of this tab to them. It answers how a gene of interest behaves across samples and groups.
    How to read: select a few symbols, then read the box plot and the table for their expression in each group.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: gene_name

- component: table
  title: Gene expression table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one sample with its TPM, its log2(TPM + 1) and the sample's group. It answers what a gene's expression is in a given sample and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by TPM to find the most abundant genes of a sample.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_name

- component: card
  title: Samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct samples, and the bars rank the groups by how many samples they hold. It answers how the design is balanced.
    How to read: groups with one sample cannot be tested, and unequal groups weaken comparisons.
  column: sample
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: samples, by group

- component: card
  title: Mean expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean log2(TPM + 1) over every gene and sample in view, and the histogram shows how the values are distributed. It answers how the expression is spread between low and high.
    How to read: a peak near zero with a long right tail is typical, since many genes are barely expressed in any one sample. Filter to a group to compare shapes.
  column: log2_tpm
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution of expression

- component: table
  title: Merged gene counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with its estimated read count in every sample, as summarised by tximport from the Salmon quantifications. It answers what the raw counts handed to a differential expression tool look like.
    How to read: counts are estimates and may be non-integer. Compare them across samples only after normalisation, which is what the differential expression step does; use the TPM views for comparisons.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca
  title: Sample PCA
  description: |-
    Each point is a sample, placed by the first two principal components of its log2(TPM + 1) over the 500 most variable genes, and coloured by group. It answers whether samples of one group are alike and whether any sample is an outlier.
    How to read: replicates should sit next to each other and groups should separate along a component. A sample far from its group is a candidate outlier or a swap, so check its row in the table and its mapping rate before keeping it. Groups that overlap fully mean little signal between them.
    Lines and annotations: no reference line is drawn. The 500-gene selection is a fixed choice of this view.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: sample_id
    dim_1: dim_1
    dim_2: dim_2
    color: group

- component: card
  title: Groups and samples
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of groups and the ring splits the samples between them, one row per sample. It answers how the design is balanced.
    How to read: a very small slice is a group with few replicates, which limits the comparisons that follow.
  column: group
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: group
  caption: samples, by group
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Median TPM of detected genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median across samples of each sample's median TPM over the genes it detects, and the box shows the spread. It answers whether samples have a similar expression profile overall.
    How to read: a sample far from the others may carry a different library composition, for instance a dominant transcript. Compare it with the PCA.
  column: median_tpm
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Genes expressed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean count of genes per sample with at least 1 TPM, and the box shows the spread between samples. It answers how complex the transcriptome of each library is.
    How to read: a library that expresses far fewer genes than its peers of the same type is a candidate for degradation or low depth. Salmon sets no minimum, so compare within the run.
    Lines and annotations: a gene counts as expressed at TPM of 1 or more, a fixed convention of this view and not a Salmon cut-off.
  column: genes_expressed
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Genes detected
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean count of genes per sample with any signal (TPM above 0), and the histogram shows how samples spread. It answers how many genes each library touches at all.
    How to read: detection grows with depth, so a low value can simply mean few reads. Read it next to the number of genes expressed.
  column: genes_detected
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: distribution across samples

- component: table
  title: Sample overview table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its principal components, its group, the genes it detects and expresses and the median TPM of its detected genes. It answers which sample to inspect.
    How to read: sort by genes expressed to find the sparsest library.

- component: card
  title: Fewest genes expressed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest count of expressed genes in any sample, with the median and the highest beside it. It answers how far the sparsest library is from the rest.
    How to read: a minimum far below the median points to an under-sequenced or degraded library. The gap matters more than the absolute number.
  column: genes_expressed
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: vertical
  caption: lowest, median and highest

- component: card
  title: Genes detected, by group
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest count of detected genes in any sample, and the bars rank the groups by their own maximum. It answers which groups carry the richest libraries.
    How to read: groups that differ much in detection may differ in depth rather than biology.
  column: genes_detected
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - min
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: group
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: the groups with most genes detected
